reason: Machine lens: all opcodes are NMOS-era (LDX #imm A2 2c/2b, STX abs 8E 4c/3b, STA abs 8D 4c/3b), real on the 65SC12. Old window 27 bytes, new 26: TAX (2c, 1b) removed, every LDA#/STA abs swapped for LDX#/STX abs and STX ora_nh for STA ora_nh at equal cost, so 2 cycles and 1 byte per key (8 keys a pass in the default build). The VIA accesses keep their order, and the cycles before each one shrink by 2 (a whole 1 MHz cycle), so each 1 MHz stretch keeps its phase. No label inside the window, no self-modified operand in it. The 1-byte shift moves &2AA7-&333E (play_sound .. sky_img0, up to SKIP unused_3400_original). A listing scan of every branch in or into that range finds none whose page crossing changes. Every indexed absolute read whose base is in it (movers_*_x_low/flags tables, the scoring tables, game_over_text+20, offsets_to_numbers_table, sky_on/h/adr/ojl/ojh/k) has a nonzero low byte, so moving the base down 1 can only remove crossings, never add them (movers_minimum_x_low-1,Y at &2BFB stops crossing for Y=5). (zp),Y reads of sky_img0 go through d_ptr = block + 8*d1 + 8*col; block lows are &7F/&EF/&5F/&CF, and reaching a page start would need odd offsets (129/17/161/49), never a multiple of 8, so no pointer goes from low byte 00 to FF. The image's other accesses (w_ptr) are writes, a fixed cost on 65C02. The assert at sky_main.6502:234 (* >= &3000) still holds (sky_on &3169 -> &3168). compiled_call's RTS moves from &3000 to &2FFF, which is harmless. No hard-coded addresses into the range in src/ (sidebyside.mjs's &3119/&3169/&3276 are the original build's). X out: dataflow marks X live after the RTS, but tracing every update_player path shows no X read before a write. The analysis is conservative at JSR add_player_bullet (LDX #5 first) and JSR consider_adding_player_bullet_or_grenade (LDX before any X use), and the skeleton path goes to consider_falling, where X is not live (in:V). A and C on exit are as before.
